gloss: to pardon; to forgive (sins or crimes)

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {赦|ゆる}していませんでした

definitions.gloss: to pardon; to forgive; to absolve
definitions.explanation: To formally forgive sins, crimes, or serious offenses. More solemn and weighty than the general-purpose 許す, often carrying religious, legal, or literary overtones.

examples.japanese: {神|かみ}がすべての{罪|つみ}を{赦|ゆる}してくださる。
{死刑囚|しけいしゅう}が{恩赦|おんしゃ}によって{赦|ゆる}された。
examples.english: The death row inmate was pardoned through an amnesty.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{長|なが}い{時間|じかん}をかけて、ようやく{過去|かこ}の{自分|じぶん}を{赦|ゆる}すことができた。
examples.english: After a long time, she was finally able to forgive her past self.

notes:
A kanji variant of ゆるす that specifically conveys pardon and absolution of sins or serious offenses. While {許|ゆる}す is the general-purpose word for "to allow, to forgive, to permit," {赦|ゆる}す is reserved for the solemn, weighty act of forgiving wrongdoing.

KANJI DISTINCTION:
- {許|ゆる}す: general "to allow, to permit, to forgive" — the default spelling
- {赦|ゆる}す: specifically "to pardon, to absolve" — used for sins, crimes, and deep personal forgiveness

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {罪|つみ}を{赦|ゆる}す: to forgive sins
- {恩赦|おんしゃ}: amnesty, pardon (contains the same kanji)
- {自分|じぶん}を{赦|ゆる}す: to forgive oneself

REGISTER:
Literary, religious, and formal. Common in Christian texts, legal contexts, and literary prose. In everyday conversation, {許|ゆる}す covers all meanings.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {許|ゆる}す: to allow, to permit, to forgive (general-purpose, much broader)
- {容赦|ようしゃ}する: to pardon, to show mercy (formal)
- {免|ゆる}す: to exempt, to release from obligation (another kanji variant)

cross_references.description: general-purpose 許す — to allow, to permit, to forgive
